parts:
Fascinated about how this is done in shiny, I wondered If one could mimick the reactive behavior of the shiny framework in a non-shiny context somehow and came up with the following approaches/solutions so far:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/25900626/reactive-object-bindings-in-a-non-shiny-context/25964811#25964811
https://github.com/Rappster/reactr

Would you happen to have/put together a little Gist that just focusses on the "nuts and bolts" with respect to reactivity so it's a bit easier to grasp? AFAIU, reactivity is based on the use of Reference Classes, but I'm really curious how you did it exactly ;-)

Thanks and keep up the awesome work!
Janko
